earnings.title: N E W S R E L E A S E
highlights: Net income of $519 million, or $2.24 per fully diluted share; adjusted net income (1) of $338 million, or $1.46 per diluted share
Net cash provided by operating activities of $1,177 million, driven by operational performance and liquids revenue
Repurchased $305 million of common stock in the third quarter; year-to-date repurchases total approximately $900 million or 4% of shares outstanding
During the third quarter, the Company repurchased $305 million of common stock and has $1 billion of capacity for additional repurchases under its previously announced expanded authorization.
The Company plans to pay its quarterly base dividend of $0.575 per share on December 3, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on November 12, 2026.

quotes.text: With our diversified scale, investment-grade balance sheet and coast-to-coast customer access, Expand Energy is uniquely positioned to monetize the volatility we see in the gas market today, provide advantaged supply to premium markets and capitalize on the demand growth we expect in the future.
quotes.by: President and Chief Executive Officer Danny Brown

outlook: For the full year 2026, Expand Energy expects to run 11 – 12 rigs and has updated its capital investment guidance to approximately $3 billion.
During the fourth quarter, the Company expects $80 million of marketing EBITDA, reflecting the impact of the Twin Eagle acquisition (the "Twin Eagle Acquisition"), which closed in September 2026.

items.heading: Natural gas, oil and NGL prices fluctuate widely, and lower prices for an extended period of time are likely to have a material adverse effect on our business.
items.group: Risks Related to Operating our Business

items.heading: Conservation measures and technological advances could reduce demand for natural gas and oil.
Negative public perception regarding us or our industry could have an adverse effect on our operations.
Risks related to potential acquisitions or dispositions may adversely affect our business.
If commodity prices fall or drilling efforts are unsuccessful, we may be required to record write-downs of the carrying value of our natural gas and oil properties.
If we are not able to replace reserves, we may not be able to sustain production.
